newsitem.title: NORWAY: Statoil sells Yme crude in spot market.
newsitem.headline: Statoil sells Yme crude in spot market.

text.p: Den norske stats oljeselskap AS (Statoil) said on Friday it had sold two cargoes of North Sea Yme crude on the spot market due to problems with specification.
Oil from Yme, which averages just over one cargo per month, is normally taken into Statoil's Mongstad refinery for processing.
But problems with salt water and the oil forming emulsions meant the plant was unable to handle the crude and it was sold on the spot market, Statoil spokesman Gunnar Sletvold said.

Yme, the smallest independent field to be developed on the Norwegian continental shelf, came onstream in February 1996. Since then, three other segments -- Beta East, Gamma West and Gamma South-East -- have been tied back to the main installation.
Sletvold said production should peak at around 40,000 barrels per day (bpd), but due to specification problems at one well and its subsequent closure, it had been reduced to 30,000 bpd.

To date the field has delivered 13 cargoes -- of between 800,000 and 850,000 barrels -- of the sweet, Statfjord-like crude, of which two were sold to European refiners at a discount to the North Sea benchmark Brent Blend.
Sletvold said the cargoes were split into smaller parcels. He declined to comment on the buyers identities.
"We hope the closure of the well will solve this problem and then we can resume taking the oil in to Mongstad. That will be the normal route," he said.
